CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman for: security warnings, irreversible action confirmations, multi-step sequences where fragment order risks misread, user asks to clarify or repeats question. Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service — even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. - diagnose: Disciplined diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Reproduce → minimise → hypothesise → instrument → fix → regression-test. Use when user says "diagnose this" / "debug this", reports a bug, says something is broken/throwing/failing, or describes a performance regression.

text to make it sound more natural and human-written. Based on Wikipedia's
comprehensive "Signs of AI writing" guide. Detects and fixes patterns including:
inflated symbolism, promotional language, superficial -ing analyses, vague
attributions, em dash overuse, rule of three, AI vocabulary words, negative
parallelisms, and excessive conjunctive phrases.

1	package checkpoint
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"encoding/json"
6		"fmt"
7	
8		"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6"
9	
10		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/settings"
11	)
12	
13	// OpenOptions configures Open. The zero value uses the default committed-ref
14	// topology and attaches no blob fetcher.
15	type OpenOptions struct {
16		// BlobFetcher is the CLI-level on-demand blob fetcher. The checkpoint
17		// package cannot resolve it itself, so the CLI layer injects it here and
18		// Open attaches it to the constructed store(s). nil leaves on-demand
19		// fetching off.
20		BlobFetcher BlobFetchFunc
21	
22		// RefFetcher is the CLI-level on-demand checkpoint-ref fetcher, used by the
23		// git-refs backend to resolve a checkpoint ref missing locally. nil leaves
24		// reads local-only; ignored by the git-branch backend.
25		RefFetcher RefFetchFunc
26	
27		// RemoteRefLister is the CLI-level checkpoint-ref enumerator, used by the
28		// git-refs backend's List to discover checkpoints present on the checkpoint
29		// remote but not yet local (see RemoteRefListFunc). It only fires on a
30		// context marked by WithRemoteListDiscovery. nil (or an unmarked context)
31		// leaves List local-only; ignored by the git-branch backend.
32		RemoteRefLister RemoteRefListFunc
33	
34		// Refs overrides the default committed-ref topology. A non-nil value wins,
35		// e.g. attach pins reads to Primary via PrimaryAsRead().
36		Refs *PersistentRefs
37	}
38	
39	// PrimaryIsRefs reports whether the configured primary backend is the git-refs
40	// per-checkpoint store. It centralizes the topology check so push/pre-push code
41	// does not compare backend-type strings itself. A nil config (default) is the
42	// git-branch backend, so this returns false.
43	func PrimaryIsRefs(cfg *settings.CheckpointsConfig) bool {
44		return cfg != nil && cfg.Primary.Type == BackendTypeGitRefs
45	}
46	
47	// Stores is the facade returned by Open: the persistent store plus the git-only
48	// ephemeral (shadow-branch) capability and resolved committed-ref topology.
49	type Stores struct {
50		// Persistent is the committed store that serves permanent reads and writes.
51		Persistent PersistentStore
52	
53		ephemeral EphemeralStore
54		refs      PersistentRefs
55	}
56	
57	// Open resolves the checkpoint storage topology and constructs the backing
58	// store(s). It keeps ref resolution, backend selection, and blob-fetcher wiring
59	// in one place. The primary is built through the backend registry; with no
60	// checkpoints config it resolves to the git-branch backend with no mirrors, so
61	// default behavior is unchanged. When mirrors are configured, the persistent
62	// store is a fan-out wrapper (reads from primary, best-effort writes to mirrors).
63	//
64	// Backend selection is read via settings.LoadCheckpointsConfig, which resolves
65	// like settings.Load: from the context's worktree root if set, else relative to
66	// the current working directory — not from repo. Callers opening a repository
67	// that is not the cwd should wrap ctx with that worktree root (as dispatch does).
68	// Resolution is fail-soft: a missing or unreadable settings file yields the
69	// default git-branch backend with no mirrors, preserving default behavior.
70	func Open(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, opts OpenOptions) (*Stores, error) {
71		refs := resolveOpenRefs(ctx, opts)
72		env := OpenEnv{Repo: repo, BlobFetcher: opts.BlobFetcher, RefFetcher: opts.RefFetcher, RemoteRefLister: opts.RemoteRefLister, Refs: refs}
73	
74		cfg, err := settings.LoadCheckpointsConfig(ctx)
75		if err != nil {
76			return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolve checkpoints config: %w", err)
77		}
78	
79		primaryType := resolvePrimaryType(cfg)
80		primary, err := buildPrimary(ctx, env, primaryType, primaryConfig(cfg))
81		if err != nil {
82			return nil, err
83		}
84		mirrors, err := buildMirrors(ctx, env, cfg, primaryType)
85		if err != nil {
86			return nil, err
87		}
88		writer := newFanoutStore(primary, mirrors)
89	
90		// Read routing: resolve id-keyed reads by the checkpoint's format across both
91		// git backends (a ULID lives in refs, a hex ID on the branch or a migrated
92		// ref), so a coexisting / mid-migration repo reads either format without
93		// reconfiguring. Writes still go through writer (configured primary + mirrors).
94		branchStore, refsStore, err := buildKindReadStores(ctx, env, primaryType, primary)
95		if err != nil {
96			return nil, err
97		}
98	
99		return &Stores{
100			Persistent: newKindRoutingStore(writer, branchStore, refsStore, primaryType),
101			ephemeral:  newEphemeralStore(repo, refs),
102			refs:       refs,
103		}, nil
104	}
105	
106	// buildKindReadStores returns the git-branch and git-refs read stores used for
107	// id-kind read routing, reusing the already-built primary for whichever kind it
108	// is and constructing the sibling. A non-branch/refs git-backed primary (not a
109	// real configuration today, since buildPrimary only accepts git-backed backends)
110	// yields both freshly built git stores.
111	func buildKindReadStores(ctx context.Context, env OpenEnv, primaryType string, primary PersistentStore) (branch, refs PersistentStore, err error) {
112		switch primaryType {
113		case BackendTypeGitBranch:
114			branch = primary
115			refs, err = build(ctx, env, BackendTypeGitRefs, nil)
116		case BackendTypeGitRefs:
117			refs = primary
118			branch, err = build(ctx, env, BackendTypeGitBranch, nil)
119		default:
120			if branch, err = build(ctx, env, BackendTypeGitBranch, nil); err == nil {
121				refs, err = build(ctx, env, BackendTypeGitRefs, nil)
122			}
123		}
124		return branch, refs, err
125	}
126	
127	// resolvePrimaryType returns the configured primary backend type, defaulting to
128	// the git-branch backend when none is configured.
129	func resolvePrimaryType(cfg *settings.CheckpointsConfig) string {
130		if cfg != nil && cfg.Primary.Type != "" {
131			return cfg.Primary.Type
132		}
133		return BackendTypeGitBranch
134	}
135	
136	// primaryConfig returns the primary backend's config block, if any.
137	func primaryConfig(cfg *settings.CheckpointsConfig) json.RawMessage {
138		if cfg == nil {
139			return nil
140		}
141		return cfg.Primary.Config
142	}
143	
144	// buildPrimary constructs the primary persistent store. The primary must be a
145	// git-backed backend: attach, resume, push, doctor, cleanup, and OPF all drive
146	// the primary's record through the repo and its refs, so a non-git-backed
147	// primary is rejected rather than silently half-supported.
148	func buildPrimary(ctx context.Context, env OpenEnv, typ string, raw json.RawMessage) (PersistentStore, error) {
149		if err := ValidatePrimaryBackend(typ); err != nil {
150			return nil, fmt.Errorf("checkpoints.primary: %w", err)
151		}
152		return build(ctx, env, typ, raw)
153	}
154	
155	// buildMirrors constructs the mirror writers. Each backend type may appear at
156	// most once across the topology (primary + mirrors), so a mirror cannot reuse
157	// the primary's type or another mirror's. This is the conservative form of "no
158	// two backends may write the same target": today two backends of the same type
159	// share the same refs/storage, so a duplicate type is a guaranteed collision
160	// (e.g. a git-branch mirror under a git-branch primary would double-write the v1
161	// branch). A future per-mirror config (same backend type pointed at a distinct
162	// repo/refs) could relax this; for now it is one of each type.
163	func buildMirrors(ctx context.Context, env OpenEnv, cfg *settings.CheckpointsConfig, primaryType string) ([]Writer, error) {
164		if cfg == nil || len(cfg.Mirrors) == 0 {
165			return nil, nil
166		}
167		seen := map[string]bool{primaryType: true}
168		mirrors := make([]Writer, 0, len(cfg.Mirrors))
169		for i, m := range cfg.Mirrors {
170			if _, err := lookupBackend(m.Type); err != nil {
171				return nil, fmt.Errorf("checkpoints.mirrors[%d]: %w", i, err)
172			}
173			if seen[m.Type] {
174				return nil, fmt.Errorf("checkpoints.mirrors[%d]: backend type %q is already used by the primary or another mirror; each backend type may appear at most once", i, m.Type)
175			}
176			seen[m.Type] = true
177			store, err := build(ctx, env, m.Type, m.Config)
178			if err != nil {
179				return nil, fmt.Errorf("checkpoints.mirrors[%d]: %w", i, err)
180			}
181			mirrors = append(mirrors, store)
182		}
183		return mirrors, nil
184	}
185	
186	func resolveOpenRefs(ctx context.Context, opts OpenOptions) PersistentRefs {
187		if opts.Refs != nil {
188			return *opts.Refs
189		}
190		return ResolveRefs(ctx)
191	}
192	
193	// Ephemeral returns the git-backed shadow-branch (temporary) store.
194	func (s *Stores) Ephemeral() EphemeralStore { return s.ephemeral }
195	
196	// Refs returns the resolved committed-ref topology.
197	func (s *Stores) Refs() PersistentRefs { return s.refs }

| remote `cli-checkpoints.git` (379 refs) | ❌ absent |

`git ls-remote` for it → exit 0, empty. CLI does `git fetch <that ref>` → git exits **128** ("couldn't find remote ref") → code maps best-effort fetch failure to **"checkpoint not found"**. That's the whole chain.

**Where the ID came from:** commit `4e229c0546` (HEAD of `feat/repo-mirror-use`, author **Matthias Wenz**) carries trailer `Entire-Checkpoint: 01KYSGR4W1ZATZRW47J510EZGJ`. Not your checkpoint — made on another machine / cloud trail runner.

## Why ref missing

git-refs backend (`refs_store.go:150-175`): checkpoint write does two things —
1. `SetReference` local ref (instant)
2. `enqueueForPush` → push-discovery queue, drained **best-effort at pre-push**

The **branch commit reached origin** (feat branch pushed → trailer visible to you). But the **per-checkpoint ref never reached `cli-checkpoints.git`**. On the creating machine the pre-push queue drain didn't fire or failed silently (best-effort, logs Warn, never blocks). Two decoupled pushes: branch → origin ✓, checkpoint ref → checkpoint remote ✗.

So "mixing backends?" No. "branch vs git-refs?" Routing right — data orphaned. Commit trailer points at a git-refs checkpoint that exists only on the author's local machine.

## Fix / recover

Nothing you can do locally — data not on any remote. Options:
- **Owner re-pushes**: on Matthias's machine (or the trail's cloud worktree) the ref still exists locally. Push it: `git push https://github.com/entireio/cli-checkpoints.git refs/entire/checkpoints/GJ/01KYSGR4W1ZATZRW47J510EZGJ`, or `entire hooks git pre-push` there to drain the queue.
- **Resume itself still worked** — branch switched, checkpoint fine. Only the AI session transcript restore is unavailable.

Real bug worth filing: cloud trail runner should push checkpoint refs (drain the discovery queue) before the worktree dies, else every cloud-built trail resumes with dangling checkpoints. Best-effort silent-Warn push means the failure is invisible until someone resumes.

Your config:

| Config state | git-refs push target |
|---|---|
| `checkpoint_remote` **set** (your case) | derived URL → `cli-checkpoints.git` |
| **not set** | falls back to push remote name → `origin` (cli.git) |

Flow: `resolvePushSettings` sees `checkpoint_remote` → `remote.PushURL` derives URL from your push remote's protocol (HTTPS) → `https://github.com/entireio/cli-checkpoints.git` → `checkpointURL` set → `pushTarget()` returns it. Still absent. Fetch won't help.

**Why:** `git fetch` copies refs that exist on the remote. This ref never reached `cli-checkpoints.git`, so there's nothing to fetch. `ls-remote` confirms — exit 0, empty output = ref not there. Refetching the same empty remote = same "checkpoint not found".

**Only path to recover** — the ref must first be *pushed* from where it still lives (Matthias's machine or the trail's cloud worktree):
```

  refs/entire/checkpoints/GJ/01KYSGR4W1ZATZRW47J510EZGJ
```
or run `entire hooks git pre-push` there to drain its stuck queue. After that lands, your resume fetches it fine — no special action your side.

# Checkpoint-audit tool: existing Go utilities to reuse

## 1. Checkpoint ref naming (ID → git ref)

**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/refs_naming.go`

```go
const CheckpointRefPrefix = "refs/entire/checkpoints/"                              // :19

func RefName(cid id.CheckpointID) (plumbing.ReferenceName, error)                   // :26
func ParseRef(name plumbing.ReferenceName) (id.CheckpointID, bool)                  // :43
```

- `RefName` builds `refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>` where `<shard>` = `cid.ShardFor()` and the leaf is `cid.String()`. Errors (does not return a malformed ref) when `cid.Kind() == id.KindUnknown`.
- `ParseRef` is the inverse — strips the prefix, requires exactly `<shard>/<id>` (rejects extra path segments), and re-validates that `cid.ShardFor() == shard`, so mismatched-shard or peeled (`^{}`) refs are rejected. Round-trips with `RefName`.

**Shard logic** — `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/id/id.go:134`:

```go
func (id CheckpointID) ShardFor() string {
    s := string(id)
    if len(s) < 2 { return s }
    return s[len(s)-2:]   // LAST two chars, for BOTH legacy-hex and ULID
}
```

Note: this is the **git-refs** ref namespace only. The legacy `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch tree uses a *different* layout — `(id CheckpointID) Path()` at `id.go:249` shards on the **first** two chars (`"a3/b2c4d5e6f7"`). Don't confuse the two.

## 2. Commit trailer extraction

**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go` — the package that defines and parses every Entire commit trailer.

The checkpoint trailer key and its parsers:

```go
const CheckpointTrailerKey = "Entire-Checkpoint"                                    // :42

func ParseCheckpoint(commitMessage string) (id.CheckpointID, bool)                  // :108  first trailer, validated
func ParseAllCheckpoints(commitMessage string) []id.CheckpointID                    // :124  all trailers, deduped, order-preserving (squash merges)
func ParseSession(commitMessage string) (string, bool)                              // :98
func ParseMetadata(commitMessage string) (string, bool)                             // :77
func ParseTaskMetadata(commitMessage string) (string, bool)                         // :87
func HasOPFApplied(commitMessage string) bool                                       // :249
func IsTrailerLine(line string) bool                                                // :190
func AppendCheckpointTrailer(message, checkpointID string) string                   // :237
func FormatCheckpoint(message string, cpID id.CheckpointID) string                  // :182
```

For your audit, `ParseAllCheckpoints` is the one to use when walking `git log` — it handles squash-merge commits carrying multiple `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers. The matching regex is `checkpointTrailerRegex` (`trailers.go:72`), which uses `id.CheckpointPattern` (accepts legacy 12-hex OR ULID) and then re-validates each captured token through `id.NewCheckpointID`.

**Every trailer key the CLI writes to commits** (all constants in `trailers.go:14-65`):

| Constant | Key string | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `CheckpointTrailerKey` | `Entire-Checkpoint` | checkpoint ID (12-hex or ULID) |
| `SessionTrailerKey` | `Entire-Session` | session identifier |
| `MetadataTrailerKey` | `Entire-Metadata` | metadata dir in commit tree |
| `MetadataTaskTrailerKey` | `Entire-Metadata-Task` | subagent/task metadata dir |
| `StrategyTrailerKey` | `Entire-Strategy` | strategy that created the commit |
| `AgentTrailerKey` | `Entire-Agent` | agent name (e.g. "Claude Code") |
| `SourceRefTrailerKey` | `Entire-Source-Ref` | `<branch>@<hash>` link to metadata branch |
| `BaseCommitTrailerKey` | `Base-Commit` | shadow→base code commit link |
| `CondensationTrailerKey` | `Entire-Condensation` | condensation ID (legacy) |
| `EphemeralBranchTrailerKey` | `Ephemeral-branch` | originating shadow branch |
| `OPFAppliedTrailerKey` | `Entire-OPF-Applied` | literal `true` when OPF redaction ran |

There is **no** dedicated "trail id" or "tokens" trailer. "Trail" concepts live elsewhere (`trail_cmd.go`), and token counts are read from checkpoint metadata (`checkpoint_tokens.go`), not from a commit trailer. Where persistent checkpoint commits are assembled: `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/persistent.go:1290-1299` (writes Session/Strategy/Agent/EphemeralBranch/MetadataTask trailers).

func PushURL(ctx, pushRemoteName string) (string, bool, error)                      // :143  (url, enabled, err)

func GetRemoteURLInDir(ctx, dir, remoteName string) (string, error)                 // :277

const EmptyCheckpointID CheckpointID = ""                                           // :24

func NewCheckpointID(s string) (CheckpointID, error)                                // :144  parse + validate
func MustCheckpointID(s string) CheckpointID                                        // :153  panics on invalid
func Validate(s string) error                                                       // :193
func KindOf(s string) Kind                                                          // :103  KindUnknown|KindLegacy|KindULID
func (id CheckpointID) Kind() Kind                                                  // :115

Constants for pattern-matching in free text: `Pattern` (`[0-9a-f]{12}`, :31), `CheckpointPattern` (legacy-or-ULID, :46), `MaxIDLength` (:72), `ShortIDLength` (12, :65). # Context available for a commit with a MISSING checkpoint

## Summary of the data model

- Commit trailers are defined in `cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go`. The ONLY Entire-* trailers that exist are: `Entire-Metadata`, `Entire-Metadata-Task`, `Entire-Strategy`, `Base-Commit`, `Entire-Session`, `Entire-Condensation`, `Entire-Source-Ref`, `Entire-Checkpoint`, `Ephemeral-branch`, `Entire-Agent`, `Entire-OPF-Applied`. **There is no `Entire-Trail` trailer** — trail linkage is NOT stored on the commit or in checkpoint metadata.
- Trails are explicitly documented as **branch-centric, served by the core API** (`cmd/entire/cli/trail/trail.go:1-5`): "Trails ... answer why/what ... while checkpoints answer how/when."

---

## 1. Trail linkage (commit/checkpoint → trail number/URL)

**There is no local mapping.** A trail is resolved from a **branch name** via the control-plane API. So the chain is: commit → branch → trail (network call required).

Getting the branch for your commit (all local, git-native):
- `session.State.Branch` — the branch HEAD pointed at when the session last took a turn (`cmd/entire/cli/session/state.go:136-142`). This is the intended "map a stopped session back to its branch" field.
- Or compute which branch(es) contain the commit from git directly (see section 3).

Resolving branch → trail (`cmd/entire/cli/trail_cmd.go`):
- `resolveTrailBySelector(...)` at `trail_cmd.go:229` — when no selector is given, calls `resolveTrailBranch` then `findTrailByBranch`.
- `findTrailByBranch(ctx, client, forge, owner, repo, branch)` at `trail_cmd.go:1899` — matches `t.Branch == branch`.
- `findTrailBySelector` at `trail_cmd.go:1875` — accepts a trail number, id, or branch string.
- `findTrailByNumber` at `trail_cmd.go:1906`.
- All go through `findTrail(...)` at `trail_cmd.go:1912`, which **paginates `GET /api/v1/trails/{forge}/{owner}/{repo}`** and matches client-side. There is no direct "trail by commit/checkpoint id" endpoint.

The resulting `api.TrailResource` (`cmd/entire/cli/api/trail_types.go:22-53`) gives you the trail Number, URL, Title, Status, Base, etc.

Trail number → URL:
- Prefer `TrailResource.URL` (server-supplied).
- Fallback constructor `trailWebURL(base, forge, owner, repo, number)` at `trail_cmd.go:369` → `<origin>/<forge>/<owner>/<repo>/trails/<number>`.
- `trailDisplayURL` at `trail_cmd.go:353` encapsulates the prefer-URL-else-build logic.

Repo/forge resolution: `resolveTrailRemote(ctx)` at `trail_cmd.go:1990` → `gitremote.ResolveRemoteRepo(ctx, "origin")` returns `(forge, owner, repo)`.

Trail metadata display struct: `trail.Metadata` at `cmd/entire/cli/trail/trail.go:134-153` (Number, TrailID, URL, Branch, Base, Title, Body, Status, Phase, Author, Assignees, Labels, Type, Priority, Reviewers, CreatedAt, UpdatedAt, MergedAt). Convert via `TrailResource.ToMetadata()` at `trail_types.go:62`.

---

## 2. Checkpoint metadata fields (available only when the checkpoint IS present)

Primary struct — `strategy.CheckpointInfo` at `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_types.go:33-45`:
```go
type CheckpointInfo struct {
    CheckpointID     id.CheckpointID `json:"checkpoint_id"`
    SessionID        string          `json:"session_id"`
    CreatedAt        time.Time       `json:"created_at"`
    CheckpointsCount int             `json:"checkpoints_count"`
    FilesTouched     []string        `json:"files_touched"`
    Agent            types.AgentType `json:"agent,omitempty"`      // e.g. "Claude Code"
    IsTask           bool            `json:"is_task,omitempty"`
    ToolUseID        string          `json:"tool_use_id,omitempty"`
    SessionCount     int             `json:"session_count,omitempty"`
    SessionIDs       []string        `json:"session_ids,omitempty"`
    Imported         bool            `json:"imported,omitempty"`
}
```

Author of a checkpoint (from git log on the checkpoints ref): `checkpoint.Author{Name, Email}` at `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/persistent.go:2618`, retrieved via `GetCheckpointAuthor(ctx, checkpointID)` / the `AuthorReader` interface (persistent.go ~2626-2636). NOTE: this reads the checkpoint commit, so it is unavailable when the checkpoint is missing.

Richer session-level metadata that carries the "context" fields — `session.State` at `cmd/entire/cli/session/state.go:101`:
- `SessionID` (:103), `CLIVersion` (:106), `BaseCommit`/`AttributionBaseCommit` (:111,:117), `Branch` (:142), `StartedAt`/`EndedAt` (:145,:149), `Phase`/`Kind` (:153,:157)
- `ReviewSkills`, `ReviewPrompt`, `InvestigateRunID`, `InvestigateTopic` (:163-180)
- `TurnCheckpointIDs` (:197), `LastCheckpointID` (:233)
- Token usage: `TokenUsage`, `CheckpointTokenUsage`, `SubagentTokensBaseline` — all `*agent.TokenUsage` (:295,:299,:310)
- `LastPrompt` (:351), `PromptAttributions []PromptAttribution` (:355), `PendingPromptAttribution` (:359)
- `PromptAttribution` struct at `state.go:374` (per-checkpoint user vs agent lines added/removed, per-file maps)

Ephemeral/other checkpoint carriers (also unavailable if the snapshot is gone): `checkpoint.Info` (`checkpoint/checkpoint.go:150`), `checkpoint.EphemeralCheckpointInfo` (checkpoint.go:229).

`explain` builds its checkpoint report from `checkpoint.CheckpointSummary` + `checkpoint.SessionContent` + `checkpoint.Author` + associated commits — see `formatCheckpointOutput` at `cmd/entire/cli/explain.go:1963`. These are the pieces to reuse for a report, but they all require the checkpoint to be readable.

---

## 3. Commit-derived (git-native) context — ALWAYS available even when checkpoint is missing

`entire trail resume` / `explain` already have helpers you can reuse:

Associated commits + author/date/subject: `getAssociatedCommits(ctx, repo, checkpointID, searchAll)` at `cmd/entire/cli/explain.go:1683`. It walks `repo.Log` (full DAG or first-parent) matching `trailers.ParseCheckpoint(c.Message)`, and produces `associatedCommit` (`explain.go:214`):
```go
type associatedCommit struct {
    SHA, ShortSHA, Message, Author, Email string
    Date time.Time
}
```
Populated from `c.Author.Name`, `c.Author.Email`, `c.Author.When`, and the first line of `c.Message` (explain.go:1692-1706). This is the model for pulling author/subject/date straight from the commit object.

Git author config: `GetGitAuthor(ctx) (*GitAuthor{Name,Email}, error)` at `cmd/entire/cli/git_operations.go:63` (go-git local→global with `git config` fallback). Backing helper `strategy.GetGitAuthorFromRepo(repo)`.

Default-branch / branch detection: `IsOnDefaultBranch` at `git_operations.go:108`; `isOnDefaultBranchRepo` at `:121`; `getDefaultBranchFromRemote`.

"Which branches contain a commit": there is **no existing `git for-each-ref --contains` / `branch --contains` wrapper**. The closest existing logic is `computeReachableFromMain(ctx, repo)` and `walkFirstParentCommits(...)` used inside `getAssociatedCommits` (explain.go:1733-1748) to decide reachability. `for-each-ref` usage in the repo is limited to `cmd/entire/cli/gitrepo/reftable.go` (reftable listing, not `--contains`). To find containing branches you would run git yourself (the repo shells out to git via `exec.CommandContext` as in `getGitConfigValue`, git_operations.go:94) or use go-git `repo.Log`. Trailer parsing helpers to pull checkpoint/session/agent IDs out of the commit message: `trailers.ParseCheckpoint`, `ParseAllCheckpoints`, `ParseSession`, `ParseMetadata` (`cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go:98-144`).

---

## 4. Control-plane API client (trail / findings context)

Client: `api.Client` in `cmd/entire/cli/api/client.go` (methods `Get/Post/Patch/Delete` at :135-177; `DecodeJSON`). Base URL via `api.BaseURL()`.

Trail endpoints (all require network + auth):
- List/lookup: `GET /api/v1/trails/{forge}/{owner}/{repo}` via `trailsBasePath` (`trail_cmd.go:1974`) — used by `findTrail`.
- Detail (description/body): `GET /api/v1/trails/{forge}/{owner}/{repo}/{number}` via `trailNumberPath` (`trail_cmd.go:1981`); `fetchTrailDescription` at `trail_cmd.go:378`. **Server keys detail by integer Number, not the UUID ID.**
- Enablement probe: `Client.TrailsEnabled(ctx, forge, owner, repo)` at `cmd/entire/cli/api/trails.go:13`.

Findings/review context tied to a trail (useful for a report): `loadTrailResumeFindingsContext(ctx, client, trailID)` at `cmd/entire/cli/trail_resume_cmd.go:622` → `fetchAllTrailReviewComments` / `fetchTrailReviewComments` (severity/status/freshness filters, `trailResumeTopFindingOptions` at :642). Review types in `cmd/entire/cli/api/trail_review_types.go` (`GET /api/v1/trails/{trail_id}/reviews/...`). Note these use the trail **id**, obtained from the list/detail result.

There is a second, generated OpenAPI client at `internal/coreapi/` (ogen-generated, `oas_client_gen.go` etc.), but the trail flows above use the hand-written `cmd/entire/cli/api.Client`.

**Bottom line for your tool:** trail context is NOT derivable offline — you must (a) determine the commit's branch (from `session.State.Branch` or `git branch --contains`), then (b) call the trails list API and match on `Branch` to get Number/URL/Title/Status. Everything in sections 2's `session.State` and all of section 3 is available locally without the checkpoint snapshot; the checkpoint-commit-derived fields (CheckpointInfo, checkpoint.Author, transcript/token metadata stored in the snapshot) are exactly what's lost when the checkpoint is missing from the remote.</result>

480	// Best-effort: the caller treats a fetch failure as "checkpoint not found".
481	func FetchCheckpointRef(ctx context.Context, ref plumbing.ReferenceName) error {
482		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 2*time.Minute)
483		defer cancel()
484	
485		fetchTarget := resolveCheckpointFetchTarget(ctx)
486		refSpec := "+" + ref.String() + ":" + ref.String()
487		if _, err := remote.Fetch(ctx, remote.FetchOptions{
488			Remote:   fetchTarget,
489			RefSpecs: []string{refSpec},
490			NoTags:   true,
491		}); err != nil {
492			// Redact: fetchTarget can be a remote URL with embedded credentials
493			// (CI origin URLs), and this error is logged and shown to users.
494			return fmt.Errorf("fetch checkpoint ref %s from %s: %w", ref, remote.RedactURL(fetchTarget), err)
495		}
496		return nil
497	}
498	
499	// checkpointRefListTimeout bounds the names-only ls-remote used by user-facing
500	// `entire checkpoint list` / branch explain. Kept short (not a full fetch
501	// budget): discovery is best-effort and additive — on timeout or unreachable
502	// remote the store falls back to local refs rather than stalling a previously
503	// instant command for tens of seconds.
504	const checkpointRefListTimeout = 5 * time.Second
505	
506	// ListCheckpointRefsOnRemote enumerates the per-checkpoint refs
507	// (refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>) present on the checkpoint remote, names
508	// only, via a single `git ls-remote refs/entire/checkpoints/*` — no object
509	// transfer. The git-refs store's List uses it to discover checkpoints written
510	// on another machine that have no local ref yet, then hydrates each lazily on
511	// read through FetchCheckpointRef.
512	//
513	// Scope (deliberately stricter than the on-demand read fetch):
514	//   - no checkpoint_remote configured → (nil, nil), List stays local-only
515	//     (unlike FetchCheckpointRef / remote.FetchURL, which fall back to origin);
516	//   - with checkpoint_remote configured → queries the resolved checkpoint URL
517	//     via remote.FetchURL (which can still fall through to origin in edge cases
518	//     such as settings-load failure or an underivable checkpoint URL).
519	//
520	// Resolution and ls-remote are pinned to the worktree root (not process cwd) so
521	// repo-local git config (url.*.insteadOf, credential helpers, remotes) applies.
522	func ListCheckpointRefsOnRemote(ctx context.Context) ([]plumbing.ReferenceName, error) {
523		if !remote.Configured(ctx) {
524			return nil, nil
525		}
526	
527		worktreeRoot, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx)
528		if err != nil {
529			return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolve worktree root: %w", err)
530		}
531	
532		url, err := remote.FetchURL(ctx, remote.FetchURLOptions{WorktreeRoot: worktreeRoot})
533		if err != nil {
534			return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolve checkpoint remote URL: %w", err)
535		}
536	
537		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, checkpointRefListTimeout)
538		defer cancel()
539	
540		output, err := remote.LsRemoteInDir(ctx, worktreeRoot, url, checkpoint.CheckpointRefPrefix+"*")
541		if err != nil {
542			return nil, fmt.Errorf("ls-remote checkpoint refs from %s: %w", remote.RedactURL(url), err)
543		}
544		return parseCheckpointRefNames(output), nil
545	}
546	
547	// parseCheckpointRefNames extracts the checkpoint ref names from `git ls-remote`
548	// output. Each line is "<hash>\t<refname>"; only refs under CheckpointRefPrefix
549	// are kept (the store re-validates each via ParseRef). Checkpoint refs point at
550	// commits so no peeled (`^{}`) lines appear for them; refs/tags peeled lines
551	// lack the checkpoint prefix and drop out here; any anomalous
552	// refs/entire/checkpoints/...^{} name is rejected by ParseRef downstream (the
553	// "{}" shard never matches ShardFor).
554	func parseCheckpointRefNames(output []byte) []plumbing.ReferenceName {
555		var names []plumbing.ReferenceName
556		for _, line := range strings.Split(string(output), "\n") {
557			fields := strings.Fields(line)
558			if len(fields) < 2 {
559				continue
560			}
561			name := fields[1]
562			if !strings.HasPrefix(name, checkpoint.CheckpointRefPrefix) {
563				continue
564			}
565			names = append(names, plumbing.ReferenceName(name))
566		}
567		return names

# Plan: Daily checkpoint-availability audit job

## Context

We hit a real failure: `entire trail resume 955` could not restore its session because
checkpoint `01KYSGR4W1ZATZRW47J510EZGJ` (trailer `Entire-Checkpoint:` on commit `4e229c05`,
branch `feat/repo-mirror-use`, author Matthias Wenz) exists in the commit trailer and on
`origin`, but its git-refs checkpoint ref `refs/entire/checkpoints/GJ/01KYSGR4W1...EZGJ` was
**never pushed** to the checkpoint remote `github.com/entireio/cli-checkpoints`. The git-refs
backend enqueues checkpoint refs for a best-effort pre-push drain (`enqueueForPush`,
`cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/refs_store.go:164`); when that drain never runs or fails silently,
the branch commit reaches origin while the checkpoint ref is orphaned on the creating machine.
The failure is invisible until someone tries to resume.

**Goal:** an active, scheduled (daily) audit that walks every commit created in the last 24h
across all branches, extracts each `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer, checks whether the matching ref
exists on the checkpoint remote, and — if any are missing — **fails the job** and emits a report
table (with per-commit context) to the GitHub run summary, an uploaded artifact, and Slack.

## Decisions (confirmed with user)

- **Commit scope:** all branches (`git log --branches --remotes --since=...`).
- **Engine:** a CI **shell script** (`scripts/checkpoint-audit.sh`) — no new Go/CLI surface.
- **Context per missing checkpoint:** commit-native only (no control-plane/trail API, no
  `ENTIRE_TOKEN`): checkpoint ID, commit short SHA, author, containing branch(es), date, subject.
- **Reporting:** fail the job + `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` table + uploaded artifact + Slack message.

## Design

Robustness without Go comes from leaning on git's native primitives instead of hand-rolled
regex/shard math:
- **Trailer extraction:** `git show -s --format='%(trailers:key=Entire-Checkpoint,valueonly=true)'`
  — git parses the trailer itself and returns one ID per line, handling squash-merge commits that
  carry multiple `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers.
- **Remote set:** one `git ls-remote <checkpoint-url> 'refs/entire/checkpoints/*'`; the checkpoint
  ID is the ref **leaf** (`refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<ID>` → `<ID>`), so membership is a plain
  string-set lookup — no shard arithmetic, works for both legacy-hex and ULID IDs.
- **Auth:** RFC 7617 basic header, matching the CLI (`CheckpointTokenEnvVar`,
  `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/remote/git.go:34`). Avoid creds-in-URL:
  `git -c http.extraheader="AUTHORIZATION: basic $(printf 'x-access-token:%s' "$TOKEN" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" ls-remote https://github.com/<repo>.git ...`.

### New file: `scripts/checkpoint-audit.sh`

`#!/usr/bin/env bash`, `set -euo pipefail`. Mirrors the tri-state exit convention of
`scripts/create-nightly-tag.sh` (0 = ok, non-zero = drift/error).

Inputs (env, with defaults):
- `CHECKPOINT_REPO` (default `entireio/cli-checkpoints`)
- `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN` (required to reach a private checkpoint repo)
- `AUDIT_WINDOW` (default `24 hours ago`)
- `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, `AUDIT_REPORT_FILE` (default `checkpoint-audit-report.md`) — optional sinks.

Logic:
1. Build the remote checkpoint-ID set via `ls-remote` (extraheader auth); `awk` the ref leaf into
   a sorted, deduped lookup (assoc array or `grep -Fxq` against a temp file). Fail fast (exit 2) if
   `ls-remote` errors — a broken remote must not read as "0 missing".
2. `git log --branches --remotes --since="$AUDIT_WINDOW" --format='%H'` → candidate SHAs.
3. Per SHA: read `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer value(s). For each ID not in the remote set, collect
   context in one `git show -s --format='%h%x1f%an%x1f%aI%x1f%s'` plus containing branches from
   `git branch -a --contains "$SHA" --format='%(refname:short)'` (filter to `origin/*`, strip prefix,
   dedupe). Append a report row.
4. Emit a markdown table (`Checkpoint | Commit | Author | Branch(es) | Date | Subject`) plus a summary
   line (`scanned N commits, M checkpoints, K missing`) to stdout, to `$AUDIT_REPORT_FILE`, and — if
   set — to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. Also write a machine-readable `checkpoint-audit-report.json`
   (array of missing entries) for the artifact.
5. Exit `1` when `K > 0`, `0` otherwise (`2` reserved for remote/setup errors).

Because we already know `01KYSGR4W1ZATZRW47J510EZGJ` is genuinely missing, a wide-window local run
is a built-in end-to-end fixture (see Verification).

### New file: `.github/workflows/checkpoint-audit.yml`

Modeled on `nightly.yml` (cron + App-token skeleton, SHA-pinned actions, `workflow_dispatch`
alongside `schedule`) with reporting borrowed from `e2e.yml`'s `notify-slack` job.

```yaml
name: Checkpoint Audit
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 7 * * *"      # daily 07:00 UTC (GitHub does not honor sub-daily cron reliably)
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      window: { description: "git --since window", default: "24 hours ago" }
permissions:
  contents: read
concurrency:
  group: checkpoint-audit-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```

Steps:
1. `actions/create-github-app-token@<sha>` scoped to `owner: entireio`,
   `repositories: cli-checkpoints` → the token for `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN`.
   **Prereq:** the App must be installed on `entireio/cli-checkpoints` with Contents:read. If the
   existing `HOMEBREW_TAP_APP_*` App is not installed there, add a new App secret pair (e.g.
   `CHECKPOINT_AUDIT_APP_ID` / `CHECKPOINT_AUDIT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`) or a read-only PAT secret.
2. `actions/checkout@<sha>` with `fetch-depth: 0`.
3. `git fetch --all --prune` so `--branches --remotes` sees every branch (checkout only brings the
   default branch history).
4. Run audit step (`id: audit`, `continue-on-error: true` so downstream reporting always runs):
   `scripts/checkpoint-audit.sh`, env `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN`, `AUDIT_WINDOW`, `CHECKPOINT_REPO`.
5. `actions/upload-artifact@<sha>` (`if: always()`, `retention-days: 7`) for the `.md` + `.json`.
6. Slack notify (`if: always() && steps.audit.outcome == 'failure'`): `slackapi/slack-github-action@<sha>`,
   `webhook: ${{ secrets.E2E_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL }}`, Block Kit payload with the summary line, the
   (truncated) table, and a link to the run.
7. Gate step (`if: steps.audit.outcome == 'failure'`): `exit 1` — makes the job red after reporting.

### Optional: local task

Add `[tasks."checkpoint:audit"]` to `mise.toml` that runs `scripts/checkpoint-audit.sh`, so
engineers can audit locally (`ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN=… mise run checkpoint:audit`).

## Files

- **New** `scripts/checkpoint-audit.sh` — the audit engine (git-native trailer + ls-remote diff).
- **New** `.github/workflows/checkpoint-audit.yml` — daily scheduled job + Slack/artifact reporting.
- **Edit** `mise.toml` — add `checkpoint:audit` task (optional local runner).

## Reused primitives / references

- Ref layout `refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>` — `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/refs_naming.go:19`.
- Checkpoint token auth (RFC 7617) — `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/remote/git.go:34` (`ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN`).
- CI templates — `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` (cron + App token), `.github/workflows/e2e.yml`
  (`notify-slack`, artifact upload), `scripts/create-nightly-tag.sh` (tri-state exit).
- Checkpoint remote configured in `.entire/settings.json` → `entireio/cli-checkpoints`.

## Verification

1. **Positive (known-missing fixture):** locally, with a token that can read `cli-checkpoints`:
   `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN=… AUDIT_WINDOW="120 days ago" bash scripts/checkpoint-audit.sh`
   — must list `01KYSGR4W1ZATZRW47J510EZGJ` on commit `4e229c05` / `feat/repo-mirror-use`
   (Matthias Wenz) and exit non-zero.
2. **Negative:** a tight window with no missing checkpoints exits 0 and prints an empty/"all present"
   report.
3. **Remote-error path:** run with an invalid `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN` → exits 2 (not 0), proving a
   broken remote never masquerades as "0 missing".
4. `mise run lint` (includes `lint:shellcheck`) passes on the new script; validate the workflow YAML
   (actionlint / `mise run lint` if wired) and confirm all `uses:` are SHA-pinned per repo convention.
5. Trigger the workflow via `workflow_dispatch` on a branch to confirm App-token scope, `fetch --all`,
   step summary, artifact upload, and the Slack path (temporarily widen the window to force a failure).

  ID is the ref **leaf** (`refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<ID>` → `<ID>`), so membership is a plain
  string-set lookup — no shard arithmetic, works for both legacy-hex and ULID IDs.
- **Auth:** RFC 7617 basic header, matching the CLI (`CheckpointTokenEnvVar`,
  `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/remote/git.go:34`). Avoid creds-in-URL:
  `git -c http.extraheader="AUTHORIZATION: basic $(printf 'x-access-token:%s' "$TOKEN" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" ls-remote https://github.com/<repo>.git ...`.

### New file: `scripts/checkpoint-audit.sh`

`#!/usr/bin/env bash`, `set -euo pipefail`. Mirrors the tri-state exit convention of
`scripts/create-nightly-tag.sh` (0 = ok, non-zero = drift/error).

Inputs (env, with defaults):
- `CHECKPOINT_REPO` (default `entireio/cli-checkpoints`)
- `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN` (required to reach a private checkpoint repo)
- `AUDIT_WINDOW` (default `24 hours ago`)
- `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, `AUDIT_REPORT_FILE` (default `checkpoint-audit-report.md`) — optional sinks.

Logic:
1. Build the remote checkpoint-ID set via `ls-remote` (extraheader auth); `awk` the ref leaf into
   a sorted, deduped lookup (assoc array or `grep -Fxq` against a temp file). Fail fast (exit 2) if
   `ls-remote` errors — a broken remote must not read as "0 missing".
2. `git log --branches --remotes --since="$AUDIT_WINDOW" --format='%H'` → candidate SHAs.
3. Per SHA: read `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer value(s). For each ID not in the remote set, collect
   context in one `git show -s --format='%h%x1f%an%x1f%aI%x1f%s'` plus containing branches from
   `git branch -a --contains "$SHA" --format='%(refname:short)'` (filter to `origin/*`, strip prefix,
   dedupe). Append a report row.
4. Emit a markdown table (`Checkpoint | Commit | Author | Branch(es) | Date | Subject`) plus a summary
   line (`scanned N commits, M checkpoints, K missing`) to stdout, to `$AUDIT_REPORT_FILE`, and — if
   set — to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. Also write a machine-readable `checkpoint-audit-report.json`
   (array of missing entries) for the artifact.
5. Exit `1` when `K > 0`, `0` otherwise (`2` reserved for remote/setup errors).

Because we already know `01KYSGR4W1ZATZRW47J510EZGJ` is genuinely missing, a wide-window local run
is a built-in end-to-end fixture (see Verification).

### New file: `.github/workflows/checkpoint-audit.yml`

Modeled on `nightly.yml` (cron + App-token skeleton, SHA-pinned actions, `workflow_dispatch`
alongside `schedule`) with reporting borrowed from `e2e.yml`'s `notify-slack` job.

```yaml
name: Checkpoint Audit
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 7 * * *"      # daily 07:00 UTC (GitHub does not honor sub-daily cron reliably)
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      window: { description: "git --since window", default: "24 hours ago" }
permissions:
  contents: read
concurrency:
  group: checkpoint-audit-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```

Steps:
1. `actions/create-github-app-token@<sha>` scoped to `owner: entireio`,
   `repositories: cli-checkpoints` → the token for `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN`.
   **Prereq:** the App must be installed on `entireio/cli-checkpoints` with Contents:read. If the
   existing `HOMEBREW_TAP_APP_*` App is not installed there, add a new App secret pair (e.g.
   `CHECKPOINT_AUDIT_APP_ID` / `CHECKPOINT_AUDIT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`) or a read-only PAT secret.
2. `actions/checkout@<sha>` with `fetch-depth: 0`.
3. `git fetch --all --prune` so `--branches --remotes` sees every branch (checkout only brings the
   default branch history).
4. Run audit step (`id: audit`, `continue-on-error: true` so downstream reporting always runs):
   `scripts/checkpoint-audit.sh`, env `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN`, `AUDIT_WINDOW`, `CHECKPOINT_REPO`.
5. `actions/upload-artifact@<sha>` (`if: always()`, `retention-days: 7`) for the `.md` + `.json`.
6. Slack notify (`if: always() && steps.audit.outcome == 'failure'`): `slackapi/slack-github-action@<sha>`,
   `webhook: ${{ secrets.E2E_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL }}`, Block Kit payload with the summary line, the
   (truncated) table, and a link to the run.
7. Gate step (`if: steps.audit.outcome == 'failure'`): `exit 1` — makes the job red after reporting.

### Optional: local task

Add `[tasks."checkpoint:audit"]` to `mise.toml` that runs `scripts/checkpoint-audit.sh`, so
engineers can audit locally (`ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN=… mise run checkpoint:audit`).

## Files

- **New** `scripts/checkpoint-audit.sh` — the audit engine (git-native trailer + ls-remote diff).
- **New** `.github/workflows/checkpoint-audit.yml` — daily scheduled job + Slack/artifact reporting.
- **Edit** `mise.toml` — add `checkpoint:audit` task (optional local runner).

## Reused primitives / references

- Ref layout `refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>` — `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/refs_naming.go:19`.
- Checkpoint token auth (RFC 7617) — `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/remote/git.go:34` (`ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN`).
- CI templates — `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` (cron + App token), `.github/workflows/e2e.yml`
  (`notify-slack`, artifact upload), `scripts/create-nightly-tag.sh` (tri-state exit).
- Checkpoint remote configured in `.entire/settings.json` → `entireio/cli-checkpoints`.

## Verification

1. **Positive (known-missing fixture):** locally, with a token that can read `cli-checkpoints`:
   `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN=… AUDIT_WINDOW="120 days ago" bash scripts/checkpoint-audit.sh`
   — must list `01KYSGR4W1ZATZRW47J510EZGJ` on commit `4e229c05` / `feat/repo-mirror-use`
   (Matthias Wenz) and exit non-zero.
2. **Negative:** a tight window with no missing checkpoints exits 0 and prints an empty/"all present"
   report.
3. **Remote-error path:** run with an invalid `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN` → exits 2 (not 0), proving a
   broken remote never masquerades as "0 missing".
4. `mise run lint` (includes `lint:shellcheck`) passes on the new script; validate the workflow YAML
   (actionlint / `mise run lint` if wired) and confirm all `uses:` are SHA-pinned per repo convention.
5. Trigger the workflow via `workflow_dispatch` on a branch to confirm App-token scope, `fetch --all`,
   step summary, artifact upload, and the Slack path (temporarily widen the window to force a failure).

name: Nightly Release

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 6 * * *" # 06:00 UTC daily
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write

concurrency:
  group: nightly-release-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
jobs:
  create-nightly-tag:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Generate token
        id: app-token
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.HOMEBREW_TAP_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.HOMEBREW_TAP_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          owner: ${{ github.repository_owner }}
          repositories: cli

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}

      - name: Create nightly tag
        run: |
          TAG=$(scripts/create-nightly-tag.sh) && EXIT_CODE=0 || EXIT_CODE=$?
          if [ "$EXIT_CODE" -eq 2 ]; then
            echo "Skipping — no new nightly needed."
            exit 0
          elif [ "$EXIT_CODE" -ne 0 ] || [ -z "$TAG" ]; then
            echo "::error::Failed to generate nightly tag"
            exit 1
          fi
          git tag "$TAG"
          git push origin "$TAG"

  e2e-windows:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/e2e-windows.yml
    secrets: inherit

  notify-slack:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [e2e-tests, e2e-windows]

      #   RED    — a "reliable" agent (or Windows) failed. These pass on every
      #            healthy run, so a failure here is a real regression.
      #   YELLOW — only a known-flaky agent failed. Worth investigating, but not
      #            a `main` regression. Reported so we don't lose visibility.
      - name: Classify failures
        id: classify
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Reliable tier (RED). The e2e-windows reusable job is also RED but
          # is matched separately below since it has no "(agent)" suffix.

          failed_names=$(gh api --paginate \
            "repos/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}/jobs" \
            --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name')

          red=""
          yellow=""
          while IFS= read -r name; do
            [ -z "$name" ] && continue
            case "$name" in
              *e2e-windows*) red="$red windows"; continue ;;
            esac

            agent="${name#*(}"; agent="${agent%)*}"
            case " $reliable " in
              *" $agent "*) red="$red $agent" ;;
              *)            yellow="$yellow $agent" ;;
            esac
          done <<EOF
          $failed_names
          EOF

          # Each list was built as " a b c" (leading space, space-separated).
          # Strip the leading space, then join on ", ". Empty stays empty.
          red="${red# }";       red="${red// /, }"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Audit checkpoint availability on the checkpoint remote.
#
# Walks every commit created within a time window across all branches, extracts
# each `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer, and checks whether the matching checkpoint

name: Checkpoint Audit

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 7 * * *" # 07:00 UTC daily (GitHub does not honor sub-daily cron reliably)
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      window:
        description: 'git --since window to audit'
        default: '24 hours ago'

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: checkpoint-audit-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  audit:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Generate checkpoint-repo token
        id: app-token
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.HOMEBREW_TAP_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.HOMEBREW_TAP_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          owner: ${{ github.repository_owner }}
          repositories: cli-checkpoints

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Fetch all branches
        run: git fetch --all --prune

      - name: Run checkpoint audit
        id: audit
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          AUDIT_WINDOW: ${{ github.event.inputs.window || '24 hours ago' }}
        run: scripts/checkpoint-audit.sh

      - name: Upload audit report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7
        with:
          name: checkpoint-audit-report
          path: |
            checkpoint-audit-report.md
            checkpoint-audit-report.json
          retention-days: 7

      - name: Notify Slack of missing checkpoints
        if: ${{ always() && steps.audit.outcome == 'failure' }}
        uses: slackapi/slack-github-action@dcb1066f776dd043e64d0e8ba94ca15cc7e1875d # v4.0.0
        with:
          webhook: ${{ secrets.E2E_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL }}
          webhook-type: incoming-webhook
          payload: |
            {
              "attachments": [
                {
                  "color": "#d50200",
                  "blocks": [
                    {
                      "type": "section",
                      "text": {
                        "type": "mrkdwn",
                        "text": ":red_circle: *Checkpoint audit found missing checkpoints*\n\nOne or more commits reference a checkpoint that is not on the checkpoint remote. See the report artifact for the full table.\n\n<${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}|View run details>"
                      }
                    }
                  ]
                }
              ]
            }

      - name: Fail if checkpoints are missing
        if: ${{ steps.audit.outcome == 'failure' }}
        run: |
          echo "::error::checkpoint audit reported missing checkpoints"
          exit 1

## What shipped

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `scripts/checkpoint-audit.sh` | Engine. Diffs commit `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailers vs remote checkpoint refs |
| `.github/workflows/checkpoint-audit.yml` | Daily cron (07:00 UTC) + `workflow_dispatch`; fail + summary + artifact + Slack |
| `mise.toml` | `checkpoint:audit` task for local runs |

**How it works** — git-native, no shell parsing brittleness:
- Remote set: one `git ls-remote refs/entire/checkpoints/*`; checkpoint ID = ref leaf → string-set lookup (works for ULID + legacy hex, no shard math).
- Trailers: `git show --format='%(trailers:key=Entire-Checkpoint,valueonly=true)'` — git parses, handles squash-merge multi-trailers.
- Auth: RFC 7617 basic header (matches CLI's `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN`), never creds-in-URL.
- Exit: `0` all present, `1` missing (fails job), `2` remote/setup error (broken remote never reads as "0 missing").

RFC 7617 basic-header token auth matches the CLI (`ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN`), never creds-in-URL.

- **`mise.toml`** — `checkpoint:audit` task for local runs.

## Verification

- **Positive**: 7-day window → exit 1, flagged the known-missing `01KYSGR4W1…` (and caught a second real orphan). Valid table + JSON. ~3s.
- **Remote-error**: bogus token → exit 2 (not 0).
- shellcheck / `mise run lint:shellcheck` / gofmt / gomod / YAML valid / all `uses:` SHA-pinned. No Go files touched.

## ⚠️ Prereq before enabling

The token step mints via `HOMEBREW_TAP_APP_*` scoped `repositories: cli-checkpoints`. **That GitHub App must be installed on `entireio/cli-checkpoints` with Contents:read.** If it isn't, add a dedicated App secret pair (or a read-only PAT) instead. Slack reuses `E2E_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL`.

name: Checkpoint Audit

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 7 * * *" # 07:00 UTC daily (GitHub does not honor sub-daily cron reliably)
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      window:
        description: 'git --since window to audit'
        default: '24 hours ago'

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: checkpoint-audit-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  audit:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Generate checkpoint-repo token
        id: app-token
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.HOMEBREW_TAP_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.HOMEBREW_TAP_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          owner: ${{ github.repository_owner }}
          repositories: cli-checkpoints

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Fetch all branches
        run: git fetch --all --prune

      - name: Run checkpoint audit
        id: audit
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          AUDIT_WINDOW: ${{ github.event.inputs.window || '24 hours ago' }}
        run: scripts/checkpoint-audit.sh

      - name: Upload audit report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7
        with:
          name: checkpoint-audit-report
          path: |
            checkpoint-audit-report.md
            checkpoint-audit-report.json
          retention-days: 7

      - name: Notify Slack of missing checkpoints
        if: ${{ always() && steps.audit.outcome == 'failure' }}
        uses: slackapi/slack-github-action@dcb1066f776dd043e64d0e8ba94ca15cc7e1875d # v4.0.0
        with:
          webhook: ${{ secrets.E2E_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL }}
          webhook-type: incoming-webhook
          payload: |
            {
              "attachments": [
                {
                  "color": "#d50200",
                  "blocks": [
                    {
                      "type": "section",
                      "text": {
                        "type": "mrkdwn",
                        "text": ":red_circle: *Checkpoint audit found missing checkpoints*\n\nOne or more commits reference a checkpoint that is not on the checkpoint remote. See the report artifact for the full table.\n\n<${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}|View run details>"
                      }
                    }
                  ]
                }
              ]
            }

      - name: Fail if checkpoints are missing
        if: ${{ steps.audit.outcome == 'failure' }}
        run: |
          echo "::error::checkpoint audit reported missing checkpoints"
          exit 1
